Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

    d = Document(filepath)

    candidates = {}
    blocks = re.split(r'(?=Candidate \d+:)', full_text)
    for block in blocks:

        if not block or 'Resumes of the candidates' in block:

            elif line.startswith('Candidate'):

            else:

        if name:

    skills_match = re.search(r'Technical Skills:\s*(.+?)(?:\n|$)', resume_text, re.IGNORECASE)
    if skills_match:
        skills = [s.strip() for s in skills_match.group(1).split(',')]
        if len(skills) >= 3:
            reqs[6] = (reqs[6][0], True)

    # 8. Recommendation Level: Exceptional/Outstanding
    if re.search(r'excellent|outstanding', eval_text, re.IGNORECASE):
        reqs[7] = (reqs[7][0], True)

    # 9. Excellence Rating: 2+ excellence mentions
    excellent_count = len(re.findall(r'excellent', eval_text, re.IGNORECASE))
    if excellent_count >= 2:
        reqs[8] = (reqs[8][0], True)

    # 10. Salary Budget: Under $150K
    sal_match = re.search(r'(?:Expected Salary:\s*\$?\s*?(\d+))', resume_text, re.IGNORECASE)
    if sal_match:
        if int(sal_match.group(1)) < 150:
            reqs[9] = (reqs[9][0], True)

    met_count = sum(1 for _, v in reqs if v)
    return reqs, met_count

# 4. Create formatted Word document for a candidate
# ============================================================
def set_cell_shading(cell, color_hex):
    shading = parse_xml(f'<w:shd {nsdecls("w")} w:fill="{color_hex}"/>')
    cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr().append(shading)

def set_cell_font(cell, text, font_name='Cambria', font_size=11, bold=False, alignment=None):
    # Clear existing runs
    for p in cell.paragraphs:
        for r in p.runs:
            r.text = ''
    paragraph = cell.paragraphs[0]
    paragraph.clear()
    run = paragraph.add_run(text)
    run.font.name = font_name
    run.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    run.bold = bold
    if alignment:
        paragraph.alignment = alignment
    else:
        paragraph.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.LEFT
    return run

def create_candidate_report(name, resume_text, eval_text, met_count, total_reqs, is_best=False):
    doc = Document()

    # === HEADING ===
    heading = doc.add_paragraph()
    heading.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    run = heading.add_run('Candidate Interview Assessment Report')
    run.font.name = 'Calibri'
    run.font.size = Pt(14)
    run.bold = True

    # === CANDIDATE NAME ===
    name_para = doc.add_paragraph()
    run = name_para.add_run(f'Candidate Name: {name}')
    run.font.name = 'Cambria'
    run.font.size = Pt(11)

    # === SECTION 1: Candidate Information ===
    section1_title = doc.add_paragraph()
    run = section1_title.add_run('Candidate Information:')
    run.bold = True
    run.font.name = 'Cambria'
    run.font.size = Pt(11)

    resume_lines = resume_text.strip().split('\n')
    for line in resume_lines:
        if line.strip():
            para = doc.add_paragraph()
            run = para.add_run(line.strip())
            run.font.name = 'Cambria'
            run.font.size = Pt(11)

    # === SECTION 2: Interviewer Evaluation ===
    section2_title = doc.add_paragraph()
    run = section2_title.add_run('Interviewer Evaluation:')
    run.bold = True
    run.font.name = 'Cambria'
    run.font.size = Pt(11)

    eval_lines = eval_text.strip().split('\n')
    for line in eval_lines:
        if line.strip():
            para = doc.add_paragraph()
            run = para.add_run(line.strip())
            run.font.name = 'Cambria'
            run.font.size = Pt(11)

    # === SECTION 3: Evaluation Conclusion ===
    section3_title = doc.add_paragraph()
    run = section3_title.add_run('Evaluation Conclusion:')
    run.bold = True
    run.font.name = 'Cambria'
    run.font.size = Pt(11)

    # Create 2x2 table
    table = doc.add_table(rows=2, cols=2)
    table.style = 'Table Grid'
    table.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER

    # Header row with D9D9D9
    hc0 = table.rows[0].cells[0]
    hc1 = table.rows[0].cells[1]
    set_cell_shading(hc0, 'D9D9D9')
    set_cell_shading(hc1, 'D9D9D9')
    set_cell_font(hc0, 'Overall Assessment', alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER)
    set_cell_font(hc1, 'Recommendation', alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER)

    # Data row with DAEEF3
    dc0 = table.rows[1].cells[0]
    dc1 = table.rows[1].cells[1]
    set_cell_shading(dc0, 'DAEEF3')
    set_cell_shading(dc1, 'DAEEF3')

    percentage = f'{met_count * 10}%'
    if is_best:
        recommendation = name
    else:
        recommendation = 'Not recommended'

    set_cell_font(dc0, percentage, alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER)
    set_cell_font(dc1, recommendation, alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER)

    filename = f'Interview_Assessment_Report_{name.replace(" ", "_")}.docx'
    doc.save(filename)
    print(f'  Created: {filename}')
    return filename

# ============================================================
# MAIN
# ============================================================

resumes = parse_resumes('/app/Candidates_resumes.docx')
print(f'  Found {len(resumes)} candidates: {list(resumes.keys())}')

print('Parsing evaluations...')
evals = parse_evaluations('/app/Interviewer_evaluation.docx')
print(f'  Found {len(evals)} evaluations: {list(evals.keys())}')

# Evaluate all candidates
candidates_eval = []
for name in resumes:
    resume_text = resumes[name]
    eval_text = evals.get(name, 'No evaluation available.')
    reqs, met_count = evaluate_candidate(name, resume_text, eval_text)
    total_reqs = len(reqs)
    print(f'\n{name}: {met_count}/{total_reqs} requirements met')
    for i, (req, met) in enumerate(reqs):
        status = 'YES' if met else 'NO'
        print(f'  {i+1}. {req}: {status}')
    candidates_eval.append((name, met_count, total_reqs, resume_text, eval_text, reqs))

# Find best candidate
best = max(candidates_eval, key=lambda x: x[1])
best_name = best[0]
print(f'\nBest candidate: {best_name} ({best[1]}/{best[2]} requirements)')

# Create documents
print('\nCreating assessment reports...')
for name, met_count, total_reqs, resume_text, eval_text, reqs in candidates_eval:
    is_best = (name == best_name)
    create_candidate_report(name, resume_text, eval_text, met_count, total_reqs, is_best)

# Write recommend.txt
with open('/app/recommend.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write(best_name)
print(f'\nrecommend.txt: {best_name}')
print('Done!')
